title: The LLM never picks the actions: how I split 'talking' from 'doing' in a Minecraft companion
author: tymuska
selftext:
I'm the solo dev behind 22Tango, a Windows desktop AI companion that plays games with you. People ask about the Minecraft part most, so here's how it's built.



The companion joins your Java world as an actual player (a Mineflayer client over LAN, no mod). It follows you, fights mobs when you say 'watch my back', gathers on request ('grab 16 oak logs'), and logs memories over time to to persist continuity. What makes it works is no language model ever selects, parameterizes or triggers an action.



\- Commands, typed or spoken (speech recognition runs locally), go through a deterministic grammar. If it can't parse you, then it can ask follow ups.

\- Reflexes, idle goals and 'assist' behavior come from pure scoring functions, and the weights depend on persona.

\- The cloud model only supplies the voice (although I'm experimenting more with skills).

\- A test scans the bot's source and fails the build if anything in the action path calls a model



Why: every failure becomes 'didn't understand' instead of 'did the wrong thing', and the whole control plane is unit-testable with no model in the loop. The bot also runs in its own process so pathfinding spikes don't stutter the desktop app, and anything that changes your world (mining, chopping) is off until you turn it on.



Even the moment that gets the biggest reaction isn't the model. Walk back past a spot where you died in an earlier session and it says, unprompted: 'Careful here — this is where it got you last time.' That's a stored death location plus a fixed line that fires within a few blocks, and only for deaths from an earlier session (otherwise it fires when you walk back to your own body). The model's job is conversation: long-term memory across sessions and its own impressions of you, all viewable and deletable in a memory window.



Stardew works too, via a SMAPI mod. There's a free alpha; links in the first comment.



Would love to hear the communities thoughts and answer any questions about this!
